jurisdiction.name: Ireland
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Ireland implements the EU AI Act through a distributed model: the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act 2026, in force since 31 July 2026, establishes a statutory AI Office of Ireland to coordinate, while statutory instruments in 2025 and 2026 designate sector regulators, including the media regulator for AI transparency duties, as market surveillance authorities. Policy follows the National Digital and AI Strategy 2030 (2026), building on the 2021 national AI strategy and its 2024 refresh, with guidelines for responsible AI use in the public service, cyber security guidelines for public-sector AI and guidance on AI in schools. The Data Protection Commission supervises large AI developers and has issued AI guidance and a 2026 report on its AI supervision, and a 2026 law allows Garda use of facial-recognition biometric analysis.
lead_institutions: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Bills on AI companion services for children and on deepfake intimate images are still pending and are listed as leads.

instruments.english_title: Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act 2026 (No. 31 of 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: Houses of the Oireachtas (sponsored by the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment)
instruments.current_status: Signed 21 July 2026 (Bill No. 69 of 2026, Government bill, status 'Enacted' on the Oireachtas register). Commenced on 31 July 2026 by the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act 2026 (Commencement) Order 2026 (S.I. No. 403 of 2026), except paragraphs (a) and (e) of the definition of 'applicable market surveillance authority' in section 78; 31 July 2026 is the establishment day of Oifig IS na hÉireann (S.I. No. 404 of 2026). Irish short title: An tAcht um an Intleacht Shaorga a Rialáil, 2026. Gives effect to the General Scheme published on 4 February 2026.
instruments.summary: Act giving further effect to the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) in Ireland: it establishes Oifig IS na hÉireann (the AI Office of Ireland) as a statutory body with a board and chief executive to coordinate competent authorities, act as single point of contact, keep an AI register, run the AI regulatory sandbox and real-world testing arrangements, and promote AI innovation and literacy. It sets general obligations and co-operation duties for the distributed market surveillance authorities, gives authorised officers powers (contravention and prohibition notices, seizure, content removal), and creates an adjudication and administrative-fines procedure; it amends the Central Bank Act 1942, the Communications Regulation Act 2002, the Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2014 and the Freedom of Information Act 2014.

instruments.english_title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence Innovation: Insights from the Data Protection Commission's Supervision of AI (2021-2025)
instruments.summary: Report by the DPC's Technology Multinational Supervision Unit on its supervision of about 180 AI products and services (LLMs, recommender systems, facial recognition, age assurance, agents) at companies such as Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, TikTok and X between 2021 and 2025. It creates no legal obligations.

leads.english_title: A Sectoral Study on Artificial Intelligence in Enterprise in Ireland
leads.issuing_authority: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment
leads.note: Study prepared by Accenture for the Department; announced 13 October 2026 (https://enterprise.gov.ie/en/publications/a-sectoral-study-on-ai-in-enterprise-in-ireland.html).
